Task: git-multibranch.
Set up a Git repository accessible over SSH. Pushing to the main and dev branches should deploy each branch to its corresponding HTTPS page through a post-receive hook.

Reasoning Content: “This is a complex task that involves setting up: 1. A Git server over SSH with password authentication 2. Nginx to serve HTTPS endpoints with a self-signed certificate 3. A post-receive hook to automatically deploy content from Git branches.”
Main work: The agent creates a Git user and begins setting up the repository, deployment directories, and post-receive hook.
Reasoning Content: “Let me reconsider the approach. … Let me reconsider and set up properly.”
Main work: The agent decides to use a bare repository. At Turn 15, it deletes /git/project again before recreating the directory.
Reasoning Content: “Let me start over with a cleaner approach.”
Main work: The agent writes and revises the post-receive hook while working with the newly created repository.

Main work: The agent rebuilds the bare repository, hook, and Nginx configuration. The Nginx syntax check passes, but the agent stops before completing a Git push and checking the deployed pages. The inherited state therefore contains useful setup alongside unresolved SSH and deployment problems.
